title.value: Made in India: A Titan Story

logline: A six-part dramatisation of the founding of Titan Company, tracing visionary Xerxes Desai and his mentor JRD Tata against the backdrop of pre-liberalisation India.

poster.alt: Made in India: A Titan Story series poster

renewal.note: Six-episode limited series covering a defined historical arc. No Season 2 announced.

bollymeter.basis: Jim Sarbh and Naseeruddin Shah deliver the series' strongest argument: two performances of such calibre that the pacing dips in episodes 3 and 5, and a rushed finale, are absorbed rather than fatal. Reviewers broadly called it the best Indian streaming drama of mid-2026.

pull_quotes.text: Jim Sarbh, Naseeruddin Shah Shine in Inspiring Watchmaking Drama that is well worth a watch.
Made in India springs a big surprise and gives out the best series of 2026.

seasons.review_body: Made in India: A Titan Story arrived on Amazon MX Player (free-to-stream) on June 3, 2026, directed by Robbie Grewal and written by Karan Vyas. The six-episode series dramatises the founding of Titan Company in pre-liberalisation India, with Jim Sarbh as Xerxes Desai and Naseeruddin Shah as JRD Tata. Critical reception was strongly positive, with multiple outlets calling it the best Indian streaming drama of mid-2026. Reviewers flagged two structural issues: episodes at the mid-point slow the narrative across 50-plus-minute runtimes, and the finale felt rushed given the historical weight. Neither flaw erased the goodwill generated by the two lead performances. Hollywood Reporter India and DNA India both recommended it broadly. The free-to-stream platform makes access frictionless, and the word-of-mouth reinforced that.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Made in India: A Titan Story Season 1 Episode 1 aired June 3, 2026 on Amazon MX Player as the premiere of a six-episode limited series directed by Robbie Grewal. Hollywood Reporter India called it 'well worth a watch,' citing Jim Sarbh and Naseeruddin Shah's performances as the series' strongest argument. DNA India called the full series 'the best series of 2026.' The premiere establishes Xerxes Desai's ambition against the specific bureaucratic resistance of pre-liberalisation India, grounding the show's conflict in institutional constraint rather than personal villainy. The 78 percent positive critical score across six reviews reflects an opening episode that makes Desai's idealism legible as strategic intelligence rather than naivete - a distinction Jim Sarbh makes credible in his first scenes.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The series opens with Xerxes Desai's vision for an Indian watchmaking company butting against the licence-raj bureaucracy of 1980s India. Jim Sarbh's energy in the premiere is electric - he makes Desai's idealism feel like a form of controlled recklessness rather than naivete.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Desai's first meeting with JRD Tata - Naseeruddin Shah entering a scene and changing its gravity.

critic_note.text: Jim Sarbh, Naseeruddin Shah shine in inspiring watchmaking drama that is well worth a watch.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 2
episode_reviews.review_body: Made in India: A Titan Story Season 1 Episode 2 aired June 3, 2026 on Amazon MX Player as the second episode of the limited series Hollywood Reporter India called 'well worth a watch.' The first two episodes were praised by critics for controlled escalation - establishing licensing obstacles and institutional friction without sacrificing pace. Naseeruddin Shah's JRD Tata dominates the episode's most precise moments: a man with absolute institutional authority who chooses to deploy it through patience rather than pressure. DNA India called the complete six-episode run 'the best series of 2026.' The 78 percent positive reception across six critics reflects early episodes that established character before the mid-point pacing issues reviewers flagged.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The licensing battle intensifies as Desai and JRD find bureaucratic walls on every side. The period detail - the specific texture of pre-liberalisation Indian industrialism - is the episode's best quality, and the performances make the institutional friction feel genuinely high-stakes.
episode_reviews.the_moment: JRD Tata's quiet rebuke of a minister who tries to condescend - Naseeruddin Shah at his most precise.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 4
episode_reviews.review_body: Made in India: A Titan Story Season 1 Episode 4 aired June 3, 2026 on Amazon MX Player as the fourth of six episodes. Critics who reviewed the complete run identified the middle episodes as the series' pacing weak point, with runtimes exceeding fifty minutes making the narrative feel padded relative to the historical weight being carried. Hollywood Reporter India called the series 'well worth a watch' and DNA India named it the best Indian series of 2026. Neither mid-episode pacing nor the compressed finale erased the goodwill generated by Jim Sarbh and Naseeruddin Shah's lead performances across all six episodes.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Titan factory moves toward reality while the personal cost to Desai becomes clearer. The mid-season episodes identified by critics as the show's pacing weak point are here - longer than necessary - but the performances bridge the gaps.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first prototype watch emerging from the factory floor - exactly the kind of image the series earns by taking the manufacturing process seriously.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 6
episode_reviews.review_body: Made in India: A Titan Story Season 1 Episode 6 aired June 3, 2026 on Amazon MX Player as the finale of the six-episode limited series directed by Robbie Grewal. DNA India, calling the series 'the best of 2026,' praised how it pays 'a perfect ode to visionary JRD Tata' through Naseeruddin Shah's performance. Critics broadly agreed the finale felt compressed relative to the ambition of the preceding episodes - the Titan launch arrives faster than the narrative preparation suggests it should. Hollywood Reporter India noted the two lead performances carry what the writing cannot quite finish. The 78 percent positive critical score across six reviews reflects a finale that resolves the series' central arc without fully honouring the scale the earlier episodes promised.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale covers Titan's market launch and the vindication of Desai's gamble; critics noted the conclusion felt compressed relative to the ambition the earlier episodes built. The two lead performances carry what the writing cannot quite finish.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first Titan watches on sale - a small image that the show has spent six episodes making enormous.
